# United Nations: Secretaries-General and seats of UN bodies — provenance report

<!-- Generated from authored/united-nations.json by scripts/authored_decks.py. Do not edit: change the dossier and rebuild. -->

**Deck:** [`decks/united-nations.ttl`](../decks/united-nations.ttl) · **Cards:** 40 · **Licence:** [CC0 1.0 Universal](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/) · **Compiled by:** Anton Wiklund · **Created:** 2026-10-04

40 cards on the United Nations as of 4 October 2026. Nine give the years in office of each Secretary-General, from Trygve Lie (1946) to António Guterres (since 2017): front the name, back the years. Thirty-one give the seat of a body of the UN system (the six principal organs, the 15 specialized agencies, the six funds and programmes, UNHCR, the IAEA, the WTO and the OPCW): front the body's name, back the city. Taken from Wikidata and checked against the United Nations Handbook 2026–27, the UN's own pages and Swedish UN sources.

## Licensing

The content sources are Wikidata, whose structured data is CC0, and the Swedish Government's communication skr. 2024/25:61, which as a statement of a Swedish authority is not protected by copyright (upphovsrättslagen 9 §). From Wikidata come the Secretaries-General and their years, the bodies, their classes and seats, the English names and the Swedish names except two, and the facts in most notes; from skr. 2024/25:61 the Swedish names of UNIDO and UNESCO, which Wikidata lacks. The deck is therefore CC0 1.0 like the rest of the library. Every other source was used for verification only: the UN Handbook 2026–27 (Crown copyright reserved), the UN's pages (Ask DAG, Main Bodies, the UN in Türkiye and UNRIC's Swedish page, all under the UN's non-commercial Terms of Use), UNFPA's page (all rights reserved), Security Council Report (copyright Security Council Report) and the WTO (all rights reserved) and the Swedish Wikipedia (CC BY-SA 4.0) confirmed facts and names, and no wording, layout or list was copied from them; the three facts that only they state (the Trusteeship Council's suspension, UNFPA's partial move and the IAEA, WTO and OPCW being related organizations) are given as bare facts in the compiler's own words. The selection is the compiler's: complete official categories (all Secretaries-General, and the six principal organs, the specialized agencies and the funds and programmes as Wikidata's classes list them) plus four bodies chosen for this deck. The fronts, the notes and the description are the compiler's own wording. Quotations in the provenance report's evidence remain under their sources' licences and are given only to make the checks verifiable.

## Method

1. Who did the work: Anton Wiklund compiled this deck with the help of AI agents (Claude, by Anthropic), which did the research, drafting and cross-checking at his direction. The cards were checked by machine (live Wikidata and the app's SHACL and DCAT-AP validators) and in independent review rounds by further Claude agents, each logged under Quality control with its findings and how they were resolved. Anton Wiklund reviews every deck in full before it is released.
2. 1. Secretaries-General (Wikidata, query 1): every non-deprecated P39 (position held) statement whose value is Secretary-General of the United Nations (Q81066), with its P1545 (series ordinal), P580 (start time) and P582 (end time) qualifiers, its rank and the English and Swedish labels, was fetched as CSV from the Wikidata Query Service (run.sh). It returned ten statements: nine with the ordinals 1 to 9 (Trygve Lie to António Guterres, the last of preferred rank and without an end time) and Gladwyn Jebb (Q1275) without an ordinal, 1945-10-24 to 1946-02-02, who served only as acting Secretary-General before the first was appointed (Ask DAG: "served as Acting Secretary-General from 24 October 1945 - 1 February 1946") and is left out.
3. 2. Years in office: each card's back is the first and last year of the term, from the P580 and P582 qualifiers, compared by hand with the UN's own list on Ask DAG (Dag Hammarskjöld Library, query 12), with the list "Secretaries-General" of the United Nations Handbook 2026–27 (p. 198, "installed" dates, query 16) and with the table of the Swedish Wikipedia article "Förenta nationernas generalsekreterare" (query 11). All four agree on every year except Ban Ki-moon's last: Wikidata's P582 is 2017-01-01 (the day his successor took office), the UN list and the Swedish table say 2016 and the Handbook has António Guterres installed on 1 January 2017; the card says 2007–2016. For António Guterres the back is "2017–": he was still in office on 4 October 2026. Whether a successor had been appointed was checked on 4 October 2026: Wikidata has no tenth holder; the UN in Türkiye's page on the selection (query 13) says his term ends on 31 December 2026; the web searches of query 14 found no recommendation or appointment, and Security Council Report's What's In Blue of 29 September 2026 (query 24) dates the fourth Security Council straw poll to that afternoon, 29 September 2026; Security Council Report's programme of work for October 2026 (posted 1 October, query 13) says Council members "are expected to continue conducting “straw polls”". The deck therefore names no successor.
4. 3. Bodies and their seats (Wikidata, queries 2, 3, 8 and 9): the specialized agencies are the items that are instances of specialized agency of the United Nations (Q15925165) (query 2: fifteen current agencies and the defunct International Refugee Organization, left out); the funds and programmes, principal organs and other bodies were looked up by English label (query 3) or by search (search.py, query 5), and their classes (P31) and headquarters (P159) fetched (queries 8 and 9). The fifteen agencies agree with the "Specialized Agencies" of the UN Handbook's UN system chart (pp. 8–9), and the six funds and programmes (UNDP, UNEP, UNFPA, UN-Habitat, UNICEF, WFP) with its "Funds and Programmes", all six of which Wikidata classes as United Nations programmes and funds (Q139312011); the six principal organs are those of the UN's "Main Bodies" page and Wikidata's principal organ of the United Nations (Q15899789). For ICAO, the General Assembly and the International Court of Justice, P159 is a building (ICAO Headquarters, Headquarters of the United Nations, Peace Palace), and for the WTO it is the city Geneva (normal rank) and, with preferred rank, the Centre William Rappard; query 6 fetched the buildings' locations (Quartier international de Montréal; Manhattan; The Hague; Geneva); for the General Assembly, Manhattan has P131 New York City (wbgetclaims, query 27), and the builder checks this chain too, and the builder checks these cards through the building, since it sees only the best-ranked P159 values. For ICAO, the building's P276 (Quartier international de Montréal) has P131 Ville-Marie, which has P131 Montreal (wbgetentities, query 23), and the builder checks this whole chain. The rank of every body's P159 statement was re-checked live with query 21, and the class memberships with query 22 (exactly the fifteen agencies on the cards plus the defunct International Refugee Organization; exactly the six funds and programmes; exactly the six principal organs). The city on each card is the P159 city (or the building's city) and was compared with the address block of the body's entry in the UN Handbook 2026–27 ("accurate as at 1 July 2026"; the WTO, which has no address block there, with the WTO's own contact page) and, for the organs, with the UN's "Main Bodies" page (query 18). make_cards.py (query 15) read the Wikidata CSVs, the Handbook text and the other saved pages and generated every Wikidata, Handbook, Ask DAG, UNRIC and Swedish Wikipedia evidence text from them, asserting that each quoted text occurs in the saved page (the evidence added or corrected in quality-control rounds 1–3 was written by hand, patch5.py, query 26, from the pages and query results named in it); the card texts and notes were written by hand in that script.
5. 4. The Handbook was downloaded as a PDF from MFAT (query 16; the DFAT .docx of the previous edition timed out and was not used) and converted to text with pypdf (pdf2txt.py); the entries were found by searching the text for each body's name and address (ctx.py prints the lines before and after a line number). The organisations' own websites were also tried (fetch.py and fetch2.py, queries 17 and 18; WebFetch, query 14): many answered 403 or 404 or rendered nothing without JavaScript, so apart from the WTO's contact page they are not sources of this deck.
6. 5. Swedish: the Swedish names are Wikidata's sv labels or aliases (query 4) checked against the UN's Swedish page "FN:s program och fackorgan" (UNRIC, query 19) and the introductions of the Swedish Wikipedia articles (svwiki.py, query 11, each cited with its revision id). Where these differ, the deck uses the name that two of them share: "FN:s boende- och bosättningsorgan" for UN-Habitat (UNRIC, the Swedish article's introduction and a Wikidata alias, and the abbreviation list of skr. 2024/25:61, which writes it without the hyphen; the Wikidata label and the article title are "FN:s program för boende- och bebyggelsefrågor"), "Världslivsmedelsprogrammet" for WFP (Wikidata label and UNRIC), "Internationella fonden för jordbruksutveckling" for IFAD (Wikidata label and Swedish article; UNRIC writes "Internationella jordbruksutvecklingsfonden") and "Världspostföreningen" for the UPU (Wikidata label and Swedish article, which adds that it is also called Världspostunionen, UNRIC's form). Wikidata's sv labels for UNIDO and WIPO are the English names; WIPO's Swedish name "Världsorganisationen för den intellektuella äganderätten" is a Wikidata sv alias (also UNRIC's). Wikidata has no Swedish name for UNIDO and none for UNESCO's long form; these two are taken from the Government's communication to the Riksdag skr. 2024/25:61 "Internationellt bistånd genom multilaterala organisationer" (12 December 2024; public domain under upphovsrättslagen 9 §), found by searching the Riksdag's open data for the names (query 25): "FN:s organisation för industriell utveckling (UNIDO)" and "FN:s organisation för utbildning, vetenskap och kultur (Unesco)", the same forms as UNRIC's and, for UNIDO, the Swedish article's introduction. FN-förbundet's pages were looked for once (query 14) and not used; NE was not consulted. Acronyms are written in capitals in both languages, as UNRIC does, except Unesco, Unicef and Unep, which Swedish writes with only an initial capital (for Unesco and Unicef the Wikidata sv labels and the Swedish article titles; for all three skr. 2024/25:61, which writes "Unep" but "UNIDO" and "UNFPA", query 28). The organs are named "FN:s …" after their Wikidata sv labels ("FN:s sekretariat" is an sv alias; the label is "FN-sekretariatet"); the International Court of Justice is "Internationella domstolen" (sv label), not the article title "Internationella domstolen i Haag", which would give the answer away. City names: the Wikidata en and sv labels, except "New York" for New York City (Q60, sv label "New York").
7. 6. Cards: Secretaries-General: front the name (identical in English and Swedish, the Wikidata en and sv labels), front note "Years as UN Secretary-General", back the years (text in no language, zxx). Bodies: front the name with its acronym, front note "Seat (city)" / "Säte (stad)", back the city; a back note says whether it is a principal organ ("One of the six principal organs of the UN"), a specialized agency, a programme or a fund (from P31 and the name) or, for the IAEA, the WTO and the OPCW, a related organization of the UN system (the UN Handbook's chart, p. 8), and a few notes add a fact that Wikidata holds (the ICJ's Peace Palace; UN Tourism's former abbreviation UNWTO and UNHCR's alias UN Refugee Agency, both Wikidata en aliases; Hammarskjöld's country and death in office) or that a cited source states (the Trusteeship Council's suspension in 1994, UN Main Bodies; the move of some of UNFPA's headquarters functions to Nairobi, UNFPA's own page, query 24). The Swedish note texts are the compiler's own translations of the English notes ("FN:s flyktingorgan" renders "UN Refugee Agency"; it is not a Wikidata alias). Study direction front to back only: many bodies share a city.
8. 7. Machine checks: for every card the builder checks against live Wikidata the English and Swedish name (label or alias) where Wikidata has it, the P159 value (or the building and its location, for ICAO down to Montreal and for the General Assembly down to New York City), the class (P31) of the organs, agencies, funds and programmes, and the English and Swedish labels of the city; for the Secretaries-General, P39 Q81066 and the en and sv labels, and for Dag Hammarskjöld P27 Q34 and P570 1961. The years in office are qualifiers, which the builder's checks cannot reach; they rest on query 1 and the comparison in step 2. The built deck was validated with the app's SHACL and DCAT-AP validators (validate_sources.ts).

## Selection

Forty cards, as of 4 October 2026: all nine Secretaries-General of the United Nations, from Trygve Lie (1946) to António Guterres, still in office (his second term ends on 31 December 2026; no successor had been appointed by 4 October 2026); the six principal organs; the fifteen current members of Wikidata's class specialized agency of the United Nations (Q15925165), in which the World Bank Group is a single item, as it is in the UN Handbook's chart; the six members of Wikidata's United Nations programmes and funds (Q139312011); and four more bodies whose seats are often asked about: UNHCR (other UN entity) and three related organizations, the IAEA, the WTO and the OPCW. Left out: Gladwyn Jebb, acting Secretary-General 1945–1946; the defunct International Refugee Organization; UN Trade and Development (UNCTAD), renamed in 2024, for whose new name no Swedish form was found (Wikidata and the Swedish Wikipedia still have the old name, "FN:s konferens om handel och utveckling"); UN-Women and the other entities whose future was under review in the UN80 reforms (a merger of UNFPA and UN-Women was being assessed in 2026 and was not decided by 4 October 2026; UNFPA is kept, with the seat the Handbook gives as at 1 July 2026); UNRWA (headquarters in both Amman and Gaza); the Secretariat's departments and offices; regional commissions, peacekeeping missions and research institutes. The seat is the city of the body's headquarters, not its other offices (the Secretariat also has offices in Geneva, Vienna and Nairobi; UN-Habitat, for one, has a New York office); the Trusteeship Council, which suspended operation on 1 November 1994, is still a principal organ under the Charter and is kept. Headquarters can move: news reports in 2025 spoke of moving the headquarters, or some headquarters functions, of UNICEF, UNFPA and UN-Women from New York to Nairobi under the UN80 reforms; the Handbook (as at 1 July 2026) and Wikidata still give New York for UNICEF and UNFPA, and the cards give the seat as at 4 October 2026.

## Queries

**1. Every P39 statement for Secretary-General of the United Nations with ordinal, start, end, rank and labels** (Wikidata: the Secretaries-General of the United Nations (Q81066) and the bodies of the UN system)

```
sh <scratch>/run.sh q1  (curl -s -H "User-Agent: solid-memo deck research (https://github.com/antwika/solid-memo)" -H "Accept: text/csv" --data-urlencode query@<scratch>/q1.rq https://query.wikidata.org/sparql > <scratch>/q1.csv)
SELECT ?person ?en ?sv ?ordinal ?start ?end ?rank WHERE {
  ?person p:P39 ?st .
  ?st ps:P39 wd:Q81066 ; wikibase:rank ?rank .
  FILTER(?rank != wikibase:DeprecatedRank)
  OPTIONAL { ?st pq:P1545 ?ordinal }
  OPTIONAL { ?st pq:P580 ?start }
  OPTIONAL { ?st pq:P582 ?end }
  OPTIONAL { ?person rdfs:label ?en FILTER(LANG(?en) = "en") }
  OPTIONAL { ?person rdfs:label ?sv FILTER(LANG(?sv) = "sv") }
}
ORDER BY ?start

```

**2. The specialized agencies (P31 Q15925165) with their P159 and its rank and labels (Q2589094 in the VALUES was a wrong guess and matched nothing)** (Wikidata: the Secretaries-General of the United Nations (Q81066) and the bodies of the UN system)

```
sh <scratch>/run.sh q2  (curl -s -H "User-Agent: solid-memo deck research (https://github.com/antwika/solid-memo)" -H "Accept: text/csv" --data-urlencode query@<scratch>/q2.rq https://query.wikidata.org/sparql > <scratch>/q2.csv)
SELECT ?class ?classLabel ?item ?en ?sv ?hq ?hqen ?hqsv ?hqrank WHERE {
  VALUES ?class { wd:Q15925165 wd:Q2589094 }
  ?item wdt:P31 ?class .
  OPTIONAL { ?item rdfs:label ?en FILTER(LANG(?en) = "en") }
  OPTIONAL { ?item rdfs:label ?sv FILTER(LANG(?sv) = "sv") }
  OPTIONAL { ?item p:P159 ?hs . ?hs ps:P159 ?hq ; wikibase:rank ?hqrank .
             OPTIONAL { ?hq rdfs:label ?hqen FILTER(LANG(?hqen) = "en") }
             OPTIONAL { ?hq rdfs:label ?hqsv FILTER(LANG(?hqsv) = "sv") } }
  SERVICE wikibase:label { bd:serviceParam wikibase:language "en". ?class rdfs:label ?classLabel }
}
ORDER BY ?class ?en

```

**3. Funds, programmes, principal organs and other bodies looked up by English label, with P159 (UNICEF, UNDP, UNFPA and others also matched unrelated items with the same label, which were ignored)** (Wikidata: the Secretaries-General of the United Nations (Q81066) and the bodies of the UN system)

```
sh <scratch>/run.sh q3  (curl -s -H "User-Agent: solid-memo deck research (https://github.com/antwika/solid-memo)" -H "Accept: text/csv" --data-urlencode query@<scratch>/q3.rq https://query.wikidata.org/sparql > <scratch>/q3.csv)
SELECT ?name ?item ?en ?sv ?hq ?hqen ?hqsv ?hqrank WHERE {
  VALUES ?name { "United Nations Development Programme"@en "United Nations Environment Programme"@en

    "United Nations Economic and Social Council"@en "United Nations Trusteeship Council"@en
    "International Court of Justice"@en "United Nations Secretariat"@en "United Nations"@en
    "United Nations Conference on Trade and Development"@en "United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime"@en
    "Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights"@en "UNAIDS"@en "Joint United Nations Programme on HIV/AIDS"@en
    "United Nations Office for Project Services"@en "United Nations University"@en }
  ?item rdfs:label ?name .
```
